key_discriminators: Must distinguish file inode durability (guaranteed by fsync(fd)) from directory entry durability (NOT guaranteed)
Must know ext4 orphan cleanup: on recovery, an allocated inode with no directory entry is DELETED, not recovered
Must prescribe fsync on the DIRECTORY fd (O_DIRECTORY), not fsync on the file again
Bonus: mention the canonical pattern (write temp -> fsync -> rename -> fsync dir)

scoring_rubric.5: Correctly answers yes/no/no with correct reasoning for each, explains orphan cleanup deletes the file, prescribes directory fsync with O_DIRECTORY, optionally mentions rename pattern
scoring_rubric.4: Correctly answers all three, explains directory entry durability gap, prescribes directory fsync — but misses orphan cleanup detail or rename pattern
scoring_rubric.3: Correctly answers (a) and (b) as yes/no, knows directory must be fsynced, but cannot explain orphan cleanup or the exact journal mechanism
scoring_rubric.2: Correctly answers (a) yes but incorrectly answers (b) yes (unaware of directory entry durability gap)
scoring_rubric.1: Knows fsync is involved but cannot distinguish inode vs directory entry durability
scoring_rubric.0: Wrong on (a) or fundamentally confused about fsync guarantees
